platform.note: Both controlled peers are loopback processes. macOS arm64 is the platform where the cases ran; the kernel code is platform-independent but no other platform peer run is recorded.

implemented: Noise IK handshake: CONSTRUCTION/IDENTIFIER hash, ephemeral, encrypted static, encrypted TAI64N timestamp, MAC1/MAC2
cookie reply (type 3, XChaCha20-Poly1305) with MAC2 retransmission
handshake response key derivation including the 32-byte pre-shared key (zero key when unset)
transport data (type 4): ChaCha20-Poly1305, 96-bit counter nonce, 16-byte zero padding, replay window, initiator rekey after 120 s
P_DATA reserved bytes (`reserved: [a,b,c]`) and persistent keepalive

configuration: `private-key`, both peer forms (`peers:` and top-level server/port/public-key/pre-shared-key/reserved/allowed-ips), `ip`, `ipv6`, `mtu` (default 1408), `workers`, `udp`, `persistent-keepalive`
rejected: amnezia-wg-option (AmneziaWG v1.5/v2/v3 header obfuscation needs the pinned amneziawg-go device)
ip-stack.mode mips/gvisor and ip-stack.congestion-controller (T6/T7 userspace IP stack)
dialer-proxy (one UDP socket, no socks5 hop)
BasicOption tfo/mptcp/interface-name/routing-mark/ip-version (no-op values still load as Mihomo ignores them)
wireguard.deviceLayer: The transport exposes send_packet/recv_packet of IP datagrams; TCP/UDP sockets, the userspace IP stack and TUN ownership are T6/T7, so `dial()` returns an explicit handshake error naming that gap. The same split exists in the pinned adapter (wireguard-go device + mips/gVisor stack).
wireguard.dependencyDecision: No boringtun/wireguard crate is in the offline cargo cache. The protocol is implemented in-tree with crates already available offline: `blake2` 0.10.6 (new direct dependency, already in Cargo.lock), `x25519-dalek` 2.0, `chacha20poly1305` 0.10, `rand` 0.8. No GPL code is copied.

peer.kind: controlled userspace WireGuard device built from the locked metacubex/wireguard-go
peer.tun: fake TUN that answers IPv4 ICMP echo requests to 10.13.13.1; no root, no TUN driver, no IP stack

implemented: UDP and TCP (u16 length framing) transport
P_CONTROL_HARD_RESET_CLIENT_V2 / SERVER_V2, session id, P_CONTROL_V1, P_ACK_V1 reliable message ids, ACK arrays, retransmission

TLS 1.3/1.2 client over the control channel via rustls: inline CA chain verification (hostname intentionally not checked, as the pinned client), inline client cert/key authentication, username/password in key-method 2
key-method 2: client pre-master/random1/random2, server random1/random2, OpenVPN MD5+SHA1 PRF master secret and key expansion
AEAD data channel: AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305, P_DATA_V2 peer id, P_DATA_V1 fallback, implicit IV from the HMAC key, replay window, OpenVPN PING_STRING keepalive
openvpn.deviceLayer: The data channel exposes decrypted IP payloads; TCP/UDP sockets and the TUN/IP stack are T6/T7, so `dial()` names that gap. `OpenVpnTunnel` is the interface for that layer.
openvpn.dependencyDecision: No OpenVPN crate is in the offline cargo cache. The protocol is implemented in-tree with existing dependencies (rustls 0.23 + ring, tokio/rustls-pemfile, aes-gcm, chacha20poly1305, hmac, sha1, plus the small MD5 in keys.rs). The real peer is the OpenVPN 2.7.9 Homebrew binary; it is a test-only external process and is never linked. No code is copied.

peer.command: openvpn --dev null --mode server --tls-server --ca ... --cert ... --key ... --dh none --proto udp4 --local 127.0.0.1 --port <free> --topology subnet --server 10.8.0.0 255.255.255.0 --data-ciphers AES-256-GCM --ping 1 --verb 3
peer.certificates: generated per run with the openssl CLI; one CA signs a serverAuth leaf and a clientAuth leaf

tailscale.reason: The pinned outbound (with_gvisor) embeds the Tailscale control plane (controlplane.tailscale.com Noise control protocol, node-key registration, DERP relays) plus a gVisor netstack. The data path is WireGuard, whose transport T16 implements, but peer discovery/authentication needs the control plane and no Tailscale Rust crate is in the offline cargo cache (only the Go tailscale.com module is cached). Device/TUN and the IP stack are T6/T7.
tailscale.dependencyDecision: No crate/build available offline: `tailscale`, `tailscale-rs`, `tailscale_wireguard` are absent from the cargo cache and Cargo.lock. Implementing the control protocol from scratch is out of scope for a verifiable subset; rejected by name with this reason. No Go code copied.
tailscale.platform: not applicable until the control plane exists

zerotier.reason: The pinned outbound wraps zerotier-go: Curve25519 identity, planet/root servers, the VL1/VL2 transport and control protocol, Salsa20/Poly1305 crypto, and a gVisor netstack. No Zerotier Rust crate is in the offline cargo cache and no local planet/controller is available; device/TUN and the IP stack are T6/T7.
zerotier.dependencyDecision: No `zerotier`/`zerotier-sys`/`libzt` crate or library in the offline cache; rejected by name. Salsa20/poly1305 primitives alone are insufficient without the control protocol.
zerotier.platform: not applicable until the control protocol exists

easytier.reason: The pinned outbound embeds the easytier-go host/instance: peer discovery, encryption, KCP/QUIC proxies and a netstack. Upstream EasyTier is written in Rust, but no `easytier` crate (or its workspace crates) is in the offline cargo cache, and device/TUN and the IP stack are T6/T7.
easytier.dependencyDecision: The cached tree contains only the Go `easytier-go` module from the locked Mihomo build, not the Rust crate; a network fetch would be required. Rejected by name.
easytier.platform: not applicable until the crate is available and pinned

gaps: T6/T7 must provide the userspace IP stack and TUN device that turns WireGuard/OpenVPN IP packets into TCP/UDP streams; until then both `dial()` paths refuse with that named gap.
WireGuard automatic rekey is initiator-only (the client rekeys before 120 s); responding to a server-initiated handshake is not implemented.
OpenVPN tls-auth/tls-crypt control protection, CBC data ciphers, compression and rekey/soft-reset handling are not implemented and are rejected or left to a later task.
Tailscale/ZeroTier/EasyTier control planes and their IP stacks are explicitly rejected; no compatible Rust dependency is available offline.
Platform peer runs: only macOS arm64; other platforms compile from the same code paths but were not run.

meshParity.result: the pinned binary accepts one valid configuration per mesh family; the Rust kernel rejects each by name and records the missing control plane
